title: Pioneer 10 & 11
tagline: The spacecraft that opened the way to the outer planets.
kicker: A true story from deep space · 1972–2003
mystery: Who flew past Jupiter first? And where are they now?
p1.date: Earth, early 1970s. Two spacecraft are being built for a journey no machine has taken before.
p1.hello: I am Pioneer 10. And this is my sister, Pioneer 11.
p1.purpose: We were built to visit the giant planets. No spacecraft had ever been that far.
p1.weight: Each of us has a mass of about 258 kilograms.
p1.p10instruments: I carried 11 scientific instruments into the outer Solar System.
p1.p11instruments: I carried 12 instruments, including an extra triaxial fluxgate magnetometer.
p1.rtgs: We carry no solar panels. Our power comes from nuclear generators on long booms.
p2.liftoff: A rocket carried me away from Earth. I was not coming back.
p2.deployed: My booms are out. My instruments are awake. The journey begins.
p2.sister: One year later, my sister Pioneer 11 followed me into the dark.
p3.date: July 1972. No spacecraft has ever crossed the asteroid belt.
p3.belt: Nobody knew if I would survive. Would rocks and dust destroy me?
p3.hint: Drag to keep me in the safe lane.
p3.safe: Only a few hits, fewer than expected! The way to Jupiter is open.
p4.approach: Jupiter filled my view. I took about 500 pictures, even of the Great Red Spot!
p4.goal: Keep the antenna aimed at Earth!
p4.hint: Hold the button to push the signal up. The radiation fights you!
p4.data: Signal held! But the radiation beat my camera before I could see Io.
p4.heat: I took the first close-up pictures of Ganymede, a moon of Jupiter.
p4.p11date: 3 December 1974. Pioneer 11 flies past Jupiter — three times closer!
p4.slingshot: Jupiter's gravity bent my sister's path — straight toward Saturn!
p5.date: 1 September 1979. The first spacecraft at Saturn.
p5.rings: I crossed the plane of Saturn's rings. No one had ever been this close.
p5.hint: Look for a thin, faint ring outside the bright ones. Tap it!
p5.miss: That is one of the known rings. Keep looking!
p5.discovery: I found a ring no one knew about: the narrow F ring!
p5.titan: I measured Titan's temperature: minus 193 degrees. Colder than anywhere on Earth.
p5.magfield: I found Saturn's magnetic field — the first proof it existed.
p6.p10: 13 June 1983. I, Pioneer 10, cross Neptune's orbit. The first human-made object this far.
p6.p11: 23 February 1990. I, Pioneer 11, cross Neptune's orbit too.
p6.beyond: The planets became distant points. But we kept measuring. Kept sending.
p7.power: Our nuclear power was slowly fading, a little less every year.
p7.routine: On 31 March 1997, routine contact with me, Pioneer 10, ended.
p7.hint: Power is dropping. Use the buttons to keep the meter above zero!
p7.p10end: 23 January 2003. My last signal. It took 11 hours and 20 minutes to reach Earth.
p7.p10silence: I did not fall. I did not stop. I simply became too faint for Earth to hear.
p7.p11end: 30 September 1995. My last routine contact. Then 24 November — a few final minutes of data.
p7.p11silence: Earth moved beyond the direction my antenna could see. The link was gone.
p8.message: Our makers put a message on each of us: a small golden plaque.
p8.what: A man and a woman. Our solar system. A map of 14 pulsars that points to the Sun.
p8.carry: It needs no power. We carry it even after our radios have fallen silent.
p9.p10: I am Pioneer 10. I am still travelling toward the star Aldebaran.
p9.p11: I am Pioneer 11. In about four million years I will pass the star Lambda Aquila.
p9.shared: THEY HAVE GONE SILENT. THEY HAVE NOT STOPPED.
p9.bye: We have finished speaking. We have not stopped journeying.
p9.still: Pioneer 10 and 11 continue through space, carrying a message from Earth.
p9.next: Next signal: the little rover who went first…
